cases.reason: The reader's claim that numeric ties cannot differ is wrong under 2002 standard arithmetic. There, each argument expression is a 32-digit standard intermediate (8.8.1.3.2/8.8.1.3.4), and comparisons among an intrinsic function's arguments use all 32 digits (8.8.1.3.1.3 rule 1). So MIN(B*100+2 B*100+1) with B = 31 nines has two arguments equal to the least value, and RV2 requires the leftmost. Probe at --std 2002: ORD-MIN returns 2 (the second argument, not the leftmost) and MIN(...) - B*100 = 1, where 2002 gives 1 and 0. The 2023 row cannot show this: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD is not in 2023's 11.9.5.1 format (the probe is refused at 2023 with COBOL0807). This is the known 2002 standard-arithmetic defect reaching RV2's tie case.

cases.reason: The two editions word this identically, but they count a different set of currency strings. 2023 12.3.7.3 SR25 implies CURRENCY SIGN '$' PICTURE SYMBOL '$' in every source unit whose CURRENCY SIGN clauses do not name '$'. So in 2023 a unit with only CURRENCY SIGN IS '#' has two currency strings ('#' and the implied '$'), and NUMVAL-C(x) without argument-2 or LOCALE violates 2023 AR3. 2002's SPECIAL-NAMES has no implied clause (12.2.6.3 GR13: literal-7 is the currency string), so the same unit has one currency string and the call is legal in 2002. A program exists that the 2002 rule permits and the 2023 rule, read with the rule it leans on, prohibits. The 2023 row CONFORMS only through the implementor reading in docs/NUMERIC_DESIGN.md ('r25's implied $ is the picture-symbol default, not a competing string'). 2002 does not need that reading, and a correction of the 2023 row would silently break 2002. The compiler at 2002 is correct: nvc_one.cob is accepted and gives 1234.56 at 2002.
